page: Hetzner Cloud cpx31 is an x86_64 virtual server powered by the QEMU hypervisor. It features 4 shared vCPUs based on the AMD EPYC processor family running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 1.95 GB of RAM per core, and is bundled with 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. No dedicated GPUs are included in this instance type, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% of tested servers with a stress-ng single-core score of 2681.88. Multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU metrics fall within the average range. Memory performance is mixed; while cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 387.44 GB/sec, the PassMark memory score is relatively weak, placing in the bottom 25%. Storage-reliant operations, such as Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput, also register in the lower 25% tier.

From a resource density and cost-efficiency perspective, the cpx31 offers a balanced compute-to-storage ratio with its local NVMe SSD, though the shared CPU allocation represents a performance tradeoff for sustained multi-threaded workloads. This server is best suited for light compute tasks, development environments, basic web serving, and applications that benefit from fast local storage but do not require dedicated CPU threads or high memory-to-core ratios.
